source.paleography_note: CHAPTER 32 — THE GARDEN OF RIGHTEOUSNESS + TREE OF WISDOM — Aramaic 4Q206 1 xxii partial; Greek Akhmim 32:1-6 — Akhmim breaks off near end of this chapter; Ge'ez full and primary for 32:6 onward. Raphael as guide. **MAJOR CROSS-CORPUS GENESIS TREE-OF-KNOWLEDGE SITE.**

verses.text_greek: Καὶ μετὰ τὰ ἀρώματα ταῦτα κατὰ βορρᾶν ἐθεώρησα τὰ ὄρη ἑπτὰ πεπληρωμένα νάρδου καθαρᾶς καὶ εὐώδων δένδρων καὶ κιννάμωμον καὶ πιπέρεως.
verses.translit: Kai meta ta arōmata tauta kata borran etheōrēsa ta orē hepta peplērōmena nardou katharas kai euōdōn dendrōn kai kinnamōmon kai pipereōs.
verses.text_geez: ወእምድኅረ፡ ዘንቱ፡ መዐዛ፡ መንገለ፡ ሰሜን፡ ርእኩ፡ ሰብዐተ፡ አድባረ፡ ምሉዐ፡ ናርዶስ፡ ንጹሕ፡ ወዕፀወ፡ ምዑዛን፡ ወቀርፋ፡ ወበርበሬ፡
verses.notes: Northward, seven mountains of nard, fragrant trees, cinnamon, pepper. The fragrance-saturated cosmic-geography.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἐκεῖθεν ἐπορεύθην ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκρωτηρίας πάντων τῶν ὀρέων τούτων κατὰ ἀνατολὴν τῆς γῆς πορρωτέρω, καὶ διῆλθον ἐπὶ τὴν ἐρυθρὰν θάλασσαν καὶ ἐπεξήλθων αὐτῇ πορρωτέρω, καὶ διῆλθον ἐπὶ τὸν Ζωτιήλ.
verses.translit: Kai ekeithen eporeuthēn epi tas akrōtērias pantōn tōn oreōn toutōn kata anatolēn tēs gēs porrōterō, kai diēlthon epi tēn erythran thalassan kai epexēlthōn autē porrōterō, kai diēlthon epi ton Zōtiēl.
verses.text_geez: ወእምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ ላዕለ፡ አጽናፈ፡ ኵሎሙ፡ እማንቱ፡ አድባር፡ መንገለ፡ ጽባሕተ፡ ምድር፡ ርሑቀ፡ ወሐለፍኩ፡ ላዕለ፡ ባሕር፡ ቀይሕ፡ ወሐለፍኩ፡ ኀቤሁ፡ ርሑቀ፡ ወሐለፍኩ፡ ላዕለ፡ ዙቴል፡
verses.notes: **Zōtiēl** — an enigmatic angelic place-name (perhaps related to Zoti, an angel-name attested in magical literature). Crossing the Red Sea (Erythrean Sea) — eastward toward paradise.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ἦλθον πρὸς παράδεισον τῆς δικαιοσύνης· καὶ ἐθεώρουν ἐπέκεινα τῶν δένδρων τούτων δένδρα πολλὰ καὶ μεγάλα φυόμενα ἐκεῖ, ἔνδοξα καὶ μεγάλα καὶ καλά, καὶ ἔνδοξον τὸ δένδρον τῆς σοφίας, ἐξ ἧς ἐσθίουσιν καὶ γινώσκουσιν σοφίαν μεγάλην.
verses.translit: Kai ēlthon pros paradeison tēs dikaiosynēs; kai etheōroun epekeina tōn dendrōn toutōn dendra polla kai megala phyomena ekei, endoxa kai megala kai kala, kai endoxon to dendron tēs sophias, ex hēs esthiousin kai ginōskousin sophian megalēn.
verses.text_geez: ወመጻእኩ፡ ኀበ፡ ገነተ፡ ጽድቅ፡ ወእሬኢ፡ ማዕዶተ፡ እማንቱ፡ ዕፀው፡ ዕፀወ፡ ብዙኃነ፡ ወዐበይተ፡ እለ፡ ይበቍሉ፡ ህየ፡ ክቡራነ፡ ወዐበይተ፡ ወሥቡሓነ፡ ወክቡረ፡ ዕፀ፡ ጥበብ፡ ዘይበልዑ፡ እምኔሁ፡ ወያአምሩ፡ ጥበበ፡ ዐባየ፡
verses.witness_secondary: 4Q206 1 xxii partial (Milik 1976 pp. 230-232) — Aramaic of paradise + tree-of-wisdom partial
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK + CROSS-CORPUS SITE — THE TREE OF WISDOM IN THE GARDEN OF RIGHTEOUSNESS.** **Paradeisos tēs dikaiosynēs** = Garden of Righteousness, Enoch's identification of the eastern paradise. **The tree-of-wisdom (dendron tēs sophias) — those who eat from it gain great wisdom.** **Cross-corpus is dense**: Gen 2:9 (the tree of the knowledge of good and evil in the midst of the garden); Gen 3:6 ('the tree was desired to make one wise'); Prov 3:18 (Wisdom as 'a tree of life'); Prov 8 (Wisdom-Sophia as cosmic creative principle); Sir 24:13-22 (Wisdom as paradise-tree); Wisd 7-9 (Hellenistic Wisdom theology); Jewish Hokhmah / Christian Sophia / Gnostic Sophia. **The 1 Enoch identification of the tree-of-knowledge as tree-of-wisdom is the foundational Second Temple re-reading of Gen 3** — the Fall as failed pursuit of wisdom, later inverted in Christian / Gnostic readings.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ ὅμοιον ἦν τὸ δένδρον ἐκεῖνο τῇ κερατέᾳ, καὶ ὁ καρπὸς αὐτοῦ ὡσεὶ βότρυς ἀμπέλου πάγκαλος, καὶ ἡ ὀσμὴ τοῦ δένδρου διέτρεχεν πόρρωθεν.
verses.translit: Kai homoion ēn to dendron ekeino tē kerateā, kai ho karpos autou hōsei botrys ampelou pankalos, kai hē osmē tou dendrou dietrechen porrōthen.
verses.text_geez: ወይመስል፡ ውእቱ፡ ዕፅ፡ ጻፍጻፈ፡ ወፍሬሁ፡ ከመ፡ አስካለ፡ ወይን፡ ሥቡሕ፡ ጥቀ፡ ወሕብለ፡ ዕፅ፡ ይሐውር፡ እምርሑቅ፡
verses.notes: The tree resembles a carob, with fruit like a beautiful grape-cluster; fragrance carries far. The botanical specificity may reflect actual Levantine flora.

verses.text_greek: Καὶ εἶπον· Ὡς καλὸν τὸ δένδρον τοῦτο, καὶ ὡς εὐῶδες καὶ ὡραῖον ἐν τῇ ὄψει.
verses.translit: Kai eipon; Hōs kalon to dendron touto, kai hōs euōdes kai hōraion en tē opsei.
verses.text_geez: ወእቤ፡ ምንተ፡ ይሤኒ፡ ዝዕፅ፡ ወምንተ፡ ይጥዕም፡ ሕብሉ፡ ወሥቡሕ፡ ለርእይ፡
verses.notes: Enoch's exclamation at the tree's beauty. Echoes Gen 3:6 ('the woman saw that the tree was good for food and a delight to the eyes'). The verbal echo is a deliberate intertextual signal.

verses.text_geez: ወአውሥአኒ፡ ሩፋኤል፡ ቅዱስ፡ መልአክ፡ ዘምስሌየ፡ ሀሎ፡ ወይቤ፡ ዝውእቱ፡ ዕፀ፡ ጥበብ፡ ዘበልዑ፡ እምኔሁ፡ አቡከ፡ ዘትካት፡ ወእምከ፡ ዘትካት፡ ቅድሜከ፡ ወአእመሩ፡ ጥበበ፡ ወተከሥቱ፡ አዕይንቲሆሙ፡ ወአእመሩ፡ ከመ፡ ዕራቆሙ፡ እሙንቱ፡ ወተሰዱ፡ እምነ፡ ገነት፡
verses.translit: wa-ʾawśaʾanī Rufāʾēl qəddus malʾak za-məslēya hallo wa-yəbē; zə-wəʾətu ʿəḍa ṭəbab za-balʿu ʾəmənnehu ʾabuka za-təkat wa-ʾəmməka za-təkat qədmēka wa-ʾaʾmaru ṭəbaba wa-takasətu ʾaʿyəntihomu wa-ʾaʾmaru kama ʿərāqomu ʾəmuntu wa-tasaddu ʾəmənna gannat
verses.text_greek: Καὶ τότε ἀπεκρίθη μοι Ῥαφαὴλ ὁ ἅγιος ἄγγελος ὁ μετ' ἐμοῦ ὤν, καὶ εἶπεν· Τοῦτο τὸ δένδρον τῆς σοφίας ἐστὶν, ἀφ' οὗ ἔφαγον ὁ πατήρ σου ὁ ἀρχαῖος καὶ ἡ μήτηρ σου ἡ ἀρχαία, οἱ πρὸ σοῦ, καὶ ἔγνωσαν σοφίαν, καὶ ἠνεῴχθησαν οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔγνωσαν ὅτι γυμνοί εἰσιν, καὶ ἐξεβλήθησαν ἐκ τοῦ παραδείσου.
verses.witness_primary: Ge'ez (Charles 1912; Knibb 1978) — primary witness here since Akhmim ends/breaks off mid-verse
verses.witness_secondary: Akhmim Panopolitanus 32:6 partial (Black 1985 p. 62 — text breaks off in some recensions during this verse)
verses.notes: **MAJOR LENS-RISK + CROSS-CORPUS — RAPHAEL IDENTIFIES THE TREE AS THE TREE OF GENESIS 3.** Raphael reveals: this is the tree from which Enoch's 'ancient father and ancient mother' (i.e., Adam and Eve) ate — they knew wisdom, their eyes were opened, they knew they were naked, and were cast out of the garden. **Direct verbatim re-reading of Gen 3:6-7, 3:22, 3:23-24**, with the key Enochic gloss: the forbidden tree IS the tree-of-wisdom (sophia), not generic 'knowledge of good and evil'. This is the **fountainhead text** for the Sophia-tradition in Wisdom of Solomon, Sirach, Philo, NT (1 Cor 1-2 'wisdom of God'), and Gnostic / Hekhalot mystical literature. **Witness-attestation note**: Akhmim Greek breaks off in or near this verse in some manuscript states (the precise breakpoint is debated; cf. Milik 1976, Nickelsburg 2001). From this point onward in the Watchers section (32:6b through ch 36), the **Ge'ez is the only complete witness**, with sparse Aramaic 4Q205/4Q206 fragments. **The Editor will need to handle the Eden-as-tree-of-wisdom reading with care — it transforms the entire Gen 3 narrative.**
